The test image shows a tomato leaf with:
- Yellow/chlorotic discoloration across the leaf
- Multiple dark, circular lesions with **concentric rings** (bullseye/target pattern)
- Brown-black necrotic centers with visible ring patterns
- Yellowing halo around lesions

This concentric ring pattern strongly suggests **Early Blight**. Let me now view reference images from 8 different classes to confirm.
This Early_Blight reference is extremely similar to the test image - same gray background, same yellow leaf, same dark circular lesions. Now let me check other classes to rule them out.

| Class | Comparison |

| **Early_Blight** (CDDM_838) | Near-identical match: yellow leaf on gray background, dark circular lesions with concentric rings |
| Septoria_Leaf_Blotch | Small spots on green leaf, no concentric rings, no yellowing |
| Late_Blight | Large irregular brown lesion, no ring pattern |
| Bacterial_Speck | Tiny dark specks on green leaf, no rings |
| Leaf_Mold | Diffuse pale patches, no discrete ring lesions |
| Tomato_Spotted_Wilt_Virus | Ring spots on fruit, different context |
| Alternaria (stem cankers) | Microscopic spore image, not comparable |

The test image matches Early_Blight perfectly: yellowed leaf, multiple dark lesions with classic bullseye/concentric ring pattern, on a gray surface. The CDDM_838 reference is nearly identical.
